name: R-One
description: The R-One (and second-generation R-One+) is a robotic-assisted vascular interventional system developed by French medtech company Robocath (acquired by Stereotaxis). Engineered for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), R-One enables interventional cardiologists to navigate and deliver guidewires, stent catheters, and angioplasty balloons with sub-millimeter axial translation and rotation from a mobile, radiation-shielded control console using joysticks and touchscreens. The bedside robotic unit attaches to the operating table and drives a sterile single-use cassette (R-Box / R-3C), protecting operators from ionizing radiation and orthopedic fatigue by reducing radiation exposure by over 84% without compromising procedure speed or technical success. R-One received European CE mark approval in 2019 and Chinese NMPA approval through the CathBot joint venture with MicroPort MedBot, with safety and clinical efficacy validated in the multicenter European R-EVOLUTION trial.
